analysis.title: Tech Is It Too Late to Sell
key_insights: NDX is back near its long-term trendline after another round of selling. It is well below the 200-day moving average, momentum is poor, and the 21-day is crossing below the 200-day.
The report questions whether to bet against the long-term trend despite the weak short-term picture.

Goldman prime brokerage data shows US technology long/short positioning at its lowest since records began in 2016. Selling has shifted from long liquidation and de-grossing to outright short building.
CTAs have sold technology aggressively, with Nasdaq positioning close to maximum short levels. The report says the potential for a sharp squeeze is growing.
BofA Fund Manager Survey shows tech allocations at their lowest since June 2006.
In the BofA Fund Manager Survey, 52% of investors expect an AI hyperscaler to announce capex cuts within six months, up from 30% the previous month.

Goldman reports the 'Other' category of Nasdaq futures traders sold $9bn during November 3-10, a multiyear record. Futures open interest fell about $2bn per session from November 10 to 13, then rose $8.2bn during the November 16 selloff, consistent with fresh short building rather than long closing.

sector_views.rationale: Short-term technicals and sentiment are bearish, but the report asks whether to bet against the long-term trend and flags squeeze potential from record bearish positioning.

risk_factors: NDX is below its 200-day moving average with the 21-day crossing below the 200-day, and momentum is weak.
52% of fund managers expect an AI hyperscaler capex cut within six months, up from 30%.
Fresh short building could extend the selloff.
